mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE increases > 0.3pp for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous 12-month average AND CPIAUCSL > previous 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their prior 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 1% indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > 1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained INDPRO weakness below its 12-month MA by > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA by > 5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST exceeds its 12-month MA by > 5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their previous 12-month averages indicates robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 12-month average AND UNRATE > previous 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their prior 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized growth in Real Personal Income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) above 4% for two consecutive quarters signals strong household income expansion, which boosts consumption and corporate revenues, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 4% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 4% for two consecutive quarters.
